_comment: The rule registry rules-gated reads (PLAN-hard-gates.md §1, §5; §8 answer 1). One row per rule: kind `gate` names the gate that holds it, kind `prose` says why no check can. Rows with `in: ["shared"]` classify the sections of setup's shared-rules block (every CLAUDE.md with its markers); a repo path ("." is the workspace top) classifies that repo's own sections. A repo's OWN sections are classified in its own gates.json (rows without `in`), except the top's, which live here: the top is not a git repo and its owner writes only *.md. Seeded 2026-10-05 from PLAN-hard-gates.md §3 and §4; a `planned` row turns active when its gate and test land (rules-gated prints `landed:` for one). Paths are from the workspace top.

keys.section: the CLAUDE.md `## ` heading, or its start before a suffix such as " — ENFORCED"
keys.rule: a quote of the rule, found in that section after normalising (a rewritten rule fails until the row follows)
keys.in: registry rows only: "shared" and/or repo paths from the workspace top
keys.how: gate rows: rewrite | block | refuse | check (PLAN-hard-gates.md §1, strongest first)
keys.gate: gate rows: the gate's file; required unless planned; executable unless `template`
keys.test: gate rows: the gate's test file, which names the gate; required unless planned
keys.template: gate rows: true when the gate file is a template another tool installs executable
keys.status: gate rows: "planned", or absent for an active gate
keys.plan: planned rows: "PLAN-x.md §n", the plan section that schedules the gate
keys.why: prose rows: why no check can hold the rule
keys.note: anything a reader needs that the other keys cannot say
